content: Leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) is a protein encoded by the LRG1 gene in humans. Proteins in the leucine-rich repeat (LRR) family, including LRG1, are known to play critical roles in protein-protein interactions, signal transduction, cell adhesion, and cellular development. LRG1 is specifically expressed during the differentiation of granulocytes. LRG1 has been demonstrated to facilitate neovascularization, which refers to the formation of new blood vessels. This is achieved by altering the signaling of transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) in endothelial cells. LRG1 interacts with the accessory receptor endoglin and enhances signaling through the ALK1-Smad1/5/8 pathway. Clinically, the levels of LRG1 protein are significantly elevated in cases of acute appendicitis, suggesting its potential utility as a diagnostic biomarker. Furthermore, LRG1 is being investigated as a potential therapeutic target for diseases characterized by abnormal neovascularization.
